• **The period from 1966 to 1969 in India is known as the Plan Holiday because during this time the government put a pause on the Five-Year Plans that had been implemented since independence.**

• During this period, the government focused on stabilizing the economy and implementing policies to promote self-sufficiency.
 
• The Plan Holiday was followed by the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974) which focused on poverty alleviation and employment generation.

• It refers to the period when India faced a balance of payment crisis and the government implemented economic reforms under the leadership of then-Finance Minister Manmohan Singh.

• It was the Second Five-Year Plan period which focused on industrialization and agriculture.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of national income from broader to narrower concepts?

options.text: GNP at market prices - NNP at market prices - GNP at factor cost - NNP at factor cost
Personal disposable income - Personal income - GNP at market prices - GNP at factor cost
GNP at factor cost - GNP at market prices - NNP at market prices - Personal income
GNP at factor cost - NNP at factor cost- Personal income - Personal disposable income

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GNP at factor cost - NNP at factor cost- Personal income - Personal disposable income.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **GNP at factor cost:-**

 
 
• It is the broadest concept of national income as it includes all income earned by domestic factors of production, regardless of their location.
 
 
 
• **NNP at factor cost:-**
 
 
• It is a narrower concept as it deducts depreciation from GNP at factor cost. 
 
 
 
• **Personal income:-**
 
 
• It is even narrower as it only includes income received by individuals and households.
 
 
 
• **Personal disposable income:-**
 
 
• It is the narrowest concept as it deducts personal taxes and non-tax payments from personal income.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT the correctly stated component of the expenditure method of measuring national income?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Export plus import expenditure.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The expenditure method of measuring national income involves adding up the final expenditures made by households, firms, governments, and foreigners.
 
• Final investment expenditure by firms and final government expenditure are correctly stated components of the expenditure method.
 
• Final consumption expenditure by households is also a correctly stated component of the expenditure method.
 
• Export plus import expenditure, is a component of the expenditure method, but is NOT correctly stated. This should have been export-import expenditure, which is known as net exports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Final investment expenditure by firms:-**

 
 
• It refers to the amount spent by businesses on capital goods, such as machinery and equipment, that are used to produce goods and services.
 
 
 
• **Final government expenditure:-**
 
 
• It includes all spending by the government on goods and services, such as salaries of public employees and infrastructure projects.
 
 
 
• **Final consumption expenditure by households:-**
 
 
• It is the total amount spent by individuals and families on goods and services for personal use, such as food, clothing, and housing.
 
 
 
• **Net exports:-**
 
 
• These are the difference between the value of exports (goods and services sold to foreign countries) and imports (goods and services purchased from foreign countries).
